service: US pharmacy claims, payments and healthcare billing network
duration: weeks to months
what: A ransomware attack on Change Healthcare from 21 February 2024 disrupted US claims processing. UnitedHealth estimated that 90% of the more than 70,000 US pharmacies using Change's platform had to modify their electronic claims processing (company estimate, as reported by Becker's). UnitedHealth's first-quarter 2024 results reported US$872 million of unfavourable cyberattack effects on earnings (company figure; media report it as US$593 million direct response costs and US$279 million business disruption).
what_nl: Een ransomware-aanval op Change Healthcare vanaf 21 februari 2024 verstoorde de verwerking van Amerikaanse betalingsaanvragen. UnitedHealth schatte dat 90 procent van de meer dan 70.000 Amerikaanse apotheken die het platform van Change gebruiken, hun elektronische verwerking moest aanpassen (schatting van het bedrijf, zoals gemeld door Becker's). In de resultaten voor het eerste kwartaal van 2024 meldde UnitedHealth 872 miljoen dollar aan ongunstige effecten van de cyberaanval op de winst (cijfer van het bedrijf; media splitsen dat op in 593 miljoen dollar directe herstelkosten en 279 miljoen dollar bedrijfsverstoring).
cause: Change Healthcare confirmed a ransomware attack. UnitedHealth CEO Andrew Witty told a US Senate hearing that attackers got in through a server without multi-factor authentication.
cause_nl: Change Healthcare bevestigde een ransomware-aanval. UnitedHealth-ceo Andrew Witty zei op een hoorzitting in de Amerikaanse Senaat dat de aanvallers binnenraakten via een server zonder meerfactorauthenticatie.
who: UnitedHealth/Change Healthcare attributed the attack to the ALPHV (BlackCat) group, and ALPHV also claimed it. Witty testified to the US Congress that UnitedHealth paid a US$22 million ransom in bitcoin (company CEO's own testimony).

checked: Searched 19 Nov 2026: $872M confirmed in UnitedHealth Q1 2024 release; 90% pharmacies is a UnitedHealth estimate (Becker's); $22M ransom confirmed by CEO testimony (old text said not officially confirmed); unsourced US$2.87bn figure removed; Healthcare Dive source dropped (not surfaced).

service: dealer management software used by about 15,000 car dealerships in North America
duration: about two weeks, with restoration in stages from late June
what: Two attacks on CDK Global in June 2024 took its dealer systems offline, so dealerships went back to pen and paper for sales, parts and financing; restoration came in stages around the start of July. Anderson Economic Group estimated losses to dealerships at roughly US$1 billion (an outside estimate, not a company figure).
what_nl: Twee aanvallen op CDK Global in juni 2024 legden de dealersystemen plat, waardoor autodealers terugvielen op pen en papier voor verkoop, onderdelen en financiering; het herstel verliep gefaseerd rond begin juli. Anderson Economic Group schatte de verliezen van de dealers op ongeveer 1 miljard dollar (een externe schatting, geen cijfer van het bedrijf).
cause: CDK Global confirmed cyber incidents in June 2024 that took its dealer systems offline. Media reported (via sources) that ransomware was used; CDK's own wording in the sources seen was a 'cyber incident'.
cause_nl: CDK Global bevestigde cyberincidenten in juni 2024 die zijn dealersystemen platlegden. Media meldden op basis van bronnen dat ransomware werd gebruikt; CDK sprak zelf in de geraadpleegde bronnen van een 'cyberincident'.
who: Media citing sources (Reuters, Bloomberg) and researchers named the BlackSuit group (not confirmed by CDK or an authority in the sources seen). Reports that CDK paid a ransom of about US$25 million were not confirmed by CDK.

sources.title: CDK Global cyberattack impacts thousands of US car dealerships
CDK ransomware attack: car dealerships revert to paperwork
The CDK Global outage: explaining how it happened

checked: Searched: AEG ~US$1bn estimate and BlackSuit link confirmed in secondary reporting; could not confirm that CDK itself announced 'ransomware' on 24 June (Fox News claim not found), so cause downgraded C to R and reworded; ransom payment reported but unconfirmed.

service: supply-chain and workforce-scheduling software
duration: not verified; some customers reported problems for days
what: A ransomware attack on supply-chain software supplier Blue Yonder in November 2024 disrupted its customers. Starbucks said its scheduling and pay systems were hit (reports say staff pay had to be calculated manually); Morrisons reported problems with its warehouse management systems; Sainsbury's said it had contingencies in place and restored operations quickly (as reported by TechRepublic and others).
what_nl: Een ransomware-aanval op leverancier van supply-chainsoftware Blue Yonder in november 2024 verstoorde zijn klanten. Starbucks zei dat zijn rooster- en loonsystemen werden getroffen (volgens berichten moest het loon van het personeel handmatig worden berekend); Morrisons meldde problemen met zijn magazijnbeheersystemen; Sainsbury's zei dat het noodplannen had en de werking snel herstelde (zoals gemeld door TechRepublic en anderen).
cause: Reported as a ransomware attack on Blue Yonder's managed-services hosted environment; its Azure public cloud was reportedly not affected. Blue Yonder said it worked with outside cybersecurity firms.
cause_nl: Gemeld als een ransomware-aanval op de gehoste beheerde-dienstenomgeving van Blue Yonder; de publieke Azure-cloud werd naar verluidt niet getroffen. Blue Yonder zei samen te werken met externe cyberbeveiligingsbedrijven.
who: The Termite ransomware group claimed it on its leak site, saying it took 680 GB of data (claim). BleepingComputer said it could not independently confirm the link. Blue Yonder had not confirmed the claim.

sources.title: Termite ransomware, Blue Yonder disruption
Blue Yonder SaaS giant breached by Termite ransomware gang
Starbucks, supermarkets targeted in ransomware attack

checked: Searched: claim and customer impact confirmed; removed the WSJ attribution and the 'pen-and-paper' claim for Morrisons/Sainsbury's (not supported: Sainsbury's said contingencies worked); 'weeks' duration unverified so replaced.

service: social network, website and app
duration: several hours, intermittent
what: X went down repeatedly on 10 March 2025, with tens of thousands of outage reports in the US in the morning. X owner Elon Musk said the platform was hit by a 'massive cyberattack'. No cost figure was published.
what_nl: X lag op 10 maart 2025 meermaals plat, met tienduizenden storingsmeldingen in de VS in de ochtend. Eigenaar Elon Musk zei dat het platform getroffen werd door een 'massale cyberaanval'. Er werd geen kostenraming bekendgemaakt.
cause: Musk publicly said the outage was a 'massive cyberattack'. The group Dark Storm Team claimed a DDoS (flooding) attack. X has not published a technical report, so the type of attack is not independently confirmed.
cause_nl: Musk zei publiekelijk dat de storing een 'massale cyberaanval' was. De groep Dark Storm Team claimde een DDoS-aanval (overbelasting). X heeft geen technisch rapport gepubliceerd, dus het type aanval is niet onafhankelijk bevestigd.
who: Dark Storm Team (described by Check Point Research as pro-Palestinian) claimed a DDoS attack on Telegram and offered no independent proof (Security Affairs, Daily Dot). Musk said the attack came from IP addresses in the 'Ukraine area' (his statement; no evidence published). Not confirmed by X or any authority.

sources.title: Elon Musk's X DDoS attack, Dark Storm Team
Thousands of X users impacted by X outage, 'Dark Storm' claims responsibility
Dark Storm Team X outage DDoS

checked: Searched: Musk statement, Dark Storm claim and 40,000+ outage reports confirmed; Ground News aggregator removed as source; Daily Dot added; reworded Ukraine remark as Musk's own statement. Musk's X posts are the only 'company' source; not fetched.

service: online shopping, contactless payments and click-and-collect; food stock and supply systems
duration: online orders paused 46 days (from 25 April to 10 June, per Reuters); click-and-collect returned later; full recovery took months
what: M&S paused online orders in late April 2025 after a cyber attack and some shelves went empty. Reuters reported online orders resumed on 10 June after a 46-day pause; click-and-collect returned much later. M&S itself estimated the incident would cost about £300 million in operating profit, which it hoped to halve through insurance and cost controls.
what_nl: M&S schorste eind april 2025 de online bestellingen op na een cyberaanval en sommige schappen raakten leeg. Volgens Reuters werden de online bestellingen op 10 juni hervat na een pauze van 46 dagen; 'click-and-collect' kwam pas veel later terug. M&S zelf raamde de kost op ongeveer 300 miljoen pond operationele winst, die het hoopte te halveren via verzekering en kostenbeheersing.
cause: M&S confirmed a cyber attack and later confirmed customer data was stolen. Media report that DragonForce ransomware was used and that attackers entered through a third-party contractor (the TCS help-desk arrangement has been examined); the contractor route is reported, not confirmed in the sources seen.
cause_nl: M&S bevestigde een cyberaanval en later ook diefstal van klantgegevens. Media melden dat DragonForce-ransomware werd gebruikt en dat de aanvallers via een externe contractant binnenkwamen (de helpdesk-regeling met TCS werd onderzocht); die toegangsroute is gemeld, niet bevestigd in de geraadpleegde bronnen.
who: Researchers and media attribute the attack to Scattered Spider working with the DragonForce ransomware service. The UK National Crime Agency (10 July 2025) arrested four people (aged 17 to 20) over the M&S, Co-op and Harrods attacks, but did not name a group or charge them for M&S in the sources seen. Not confirmed by M&S.
europe: UK retailer; the main effects are in the UK.

Four arrested in UK over M&S, Co-op, Harrods cyberattacks
Scattered Spider arrests, UK NCA, Marks and Spencer
Harrods, M&S hit by cyberattack: what happened, who's behind it?

checked: Searched: £300M estimate by M&S, 25 April halt and 10 June restart (46 days, Reuters) confirmed; 'about seven weeks' corrected to 46 days; 'disruption into July' dropped (not re-verified). Source URLs not individually opened (WebFetch blocked by network).

service: food stores' stock supply, payments, member systems
duration: shelves affected for weeks; recovery details beyond that not verified
what: After a cyber attack in late April 2025 Co-op stores had empty shelves for weeks. In its half-year report (six months to 5 July 2025) Co-op said the attack cut sales revenue by about £206 million and operating profit by £80 million (£20 million one-off costs and £60 million lost sales). In March 2026 its full-year results estimated the direct impact of the attack at £285 million of revenue and £107 million of profit (£86 million lost margin and £21 million one-off costs); these are Co-op management estimates.
what_nl: Na een cyberaanval eind april 2025 hadden de Co-op-winkels weken lang lege schappen. In zijn halfjaarverslag (zes maanden tot 5 juli 2025) zei Co-op dat de aanval de omzet met ongeveer 206 miljoen pond en de bedrijfswinst met 80 miljoen pond verminderde (20 miljoen pond eenmalige kosten en 60 miljoen pond gemiste verkoop). In maart 2026 raamden de jaarresultaten de rechtstreekse impact op 285 miljoen pond omzet en 107 miljoen pond winst (86 miljoen pond gemiste marge en 21 miljoen pond eenmalige kosten); dat zijn schattingen van het Co-op-management.
cause: Co-op confirmed a cyber attack and that the data of all 6.5 million members was stolen. Reports say the attackers deployed DragonForce ransomware. The Financial Times first reported that Co-op had no cyber insurance; Co-op later confirmed it held no dedicated cyber insurance, though it had cover for operational disruption (as reported by Insurance Business and Insurance Insider).
cause_nl: Co-op bevestigde een cyberaanval en dat de gegevens van alle 6,5 miljoen leden werden gestolen. Volgens berichten zette de aanvaller DragonForce-ransomware in. De Financial Times meldde als eerste dat Co-op geen cyberverzekering had; Co-op bevestigde later dat het geen specifieke cyberverzekering had, maar wel dekking voor bedrijfsonderbreking (zoals gemeld door Insurance Business en Insurance Insider).
who: DragonForce claimed the attack and told the BBC it had stolen data (claim by the criminal group). Researchers link it to Scattered Spider; the NCA arrested four people on 10 July 2025 over the M&S, Co-op and Harrods attacks without naming a group. Not confirmed by Co-op.

sources.title: Co-op declares cyber attack damage cost it £206m

Empty shelves, empty coffers: Co-op pegs cyber hit at £80m
Four arrested in UK over M&S, Co-op, Harrods cyberattacks
Co-op full-year results, 26 March 2026
Co-op chose cybersecurity over insurance

checked: Searched: £206M revenue, £80M profit, 6.5M members, DragonForce/BBC confirmed; 'no cyber insurance' confirmed (FT reported, Co-op confirmed no dedicated policy, had business-interruption cover); unconfirmed '£40M more expected' and '2,300 stores' and rural-store claim removed, replaced by actual full-year figures (£285M/£107M, official release).

service: steel production at several locations
duration: restart under way at the time of the filing; end date not published in sources seen
what: Nucor, the largest US steelmaker, said in a stock-exchange filing that it temporarily and proactively halted certain production operations at various locations after unauthorised third-party access to its IT systems. It was restarting the affected operations at the time of the filing. No cost figure was given.
what_nl: Nucor, de grootste Amerikaanse staalproducent, meldde in een beursdocument dat het tijdelijk en preventief bepaalde productieactiviteiten op verschillende locaties stillegde na onbevoegde toegang tot zijn IT-systemen. Op het moment van de melding werden de getroffen activiteiten herstart. Er werd geen kostenraming gegeven.
cause: Nucor's Form 8-K reports unauthorised third-party access to certain IT systems; the company took systems offline and notified federal law enforcement. The type of attack (for example ransomware) was not stated.
cause_nl: Het 8-K-document van Nucor meldt onbevoegde toegang door een derde tot bepaalde IT-systemen; het bedrijf nam systemen offline en verwittigde de federale politie. Het type aanval (bv. ransomware) werd niet vermeld.
who: Nobody named. The filing did not attribute the incident to any group.

sources.title: Nucor Corp Form 8-K (Item 1.05)
Nucor shuts down production at multiple facilities following cyberattack

checked: Searched: SEC 8-K Item 1.05 (14 May 2025) wording confirmed: production halted at various locations, restart under way, law enforcement notified. End date not found. Later amended 8-K (20 June) mentioned by one trade outlet only; not used.

service: website and some in-store services (returns of online orders, gift cards, rewards, credit cards, per press reports)
duration: about three days (website shut 26 May, restored 29 May per Reuters)
what: Victoria's Secret shut its corporate systems and e-commerce site on 26 May 2025 as a precaution after a security incident, and restored the website on 29 May (Reuters). Some functions at its stores were disrupted and later restored, and stores stayed open. The company postponed its first-quarter earnings release, originally due 5 June, because staff lacked access to some systems and data (company, as reported).
what_nl: Victoria's Secret sloot op 26 mei 2025 uit voorzorg zijn bedrijfssystemen en webwinkel af na een beveiligingsincident en herstelde de website op 29 mei (Reuters). Sommige functies in de winkels werden verstoord en later hersteld; de winkels bleven open. Het bedrijf stelde zijn resultaten voor het eerste kwartaal, oorspronkelijk gepland op 5 juni, uit omdat medewerkers geen toegang hadden tot bepaalde systemen en gegevens (bedrijf, zoals gemeld).
cause: The company said it took systems offline as a precaution after a 'security incident' and engaged outside experts. It did not say publicly whether it was ransomware; media call it a cyber incident.
cause_nl: Het bedrijf zei dat het systemen uit voorzorg offline haalde na een 'beveiligingsincident' en externe experts inschakelde. Het zei niet publiekelijk of het om ransomware ging; media spreken van een cyberincident.
who: Nobody named. No group has claimed it and no authority has named anyone in the sources seen.

checked: Searched: dates corrected (shutdown 26 May, website back 29 May per Reuters; old text said 28 May); removed unsourced ~7% share fall and the Scattered Spider link (no source found, who S to N); cause S to R; NBC source dropped (not surfaced). Old 'returns, gift cards, rewards' service list dropped as unsourced.

service: grocery wholesale and distribution (main supplier to Whole Foods)
duration: primary electronic ordering restored within about 10 days; core systems reported back by 26 June
what: UNFI took systems offline after detecting unauthorised activity on 5 June 2025, and its filing said the incident had caused temporary disruptions to order fulfilment. Whole Foods and other grocers reported shortages and empty shelves. UNFI later said it expected the incident to reduce fiscal-2025 net sales by about US$350 to 400 million (company guidance, as reported by Teiss).
what_nl: UNFI nam systemen offline nadat het op 5 juni 2025 onbevoegde activiteit had vastgesteld; volgens het beursdocument leidde dit tot tijdelijke verstoringen bij het uitvoeren van bestellingen. Whole Foods en andere supermarkten meldden tekorten en lege schappen. UNFI zei later te verwachten dat het incident de nettoverkoop in boekjaar 2025 met ongeveer 350 tot 400 miljoen dollar zou verminderen (richtlijn van het bedrijf, zoals gemeld door Teiss).
cause: UNFI's Form 8-K reports unauthorised activity on its IT systems and containment measures; the 26 June 8-K says the company holds cyber insurance it expects to be adequate. The company did not publicly name the type of attack; observers suspected ransomware (suspected).
cause_nl: Het 8-K-document van UNFI meldt onbevoegde activiteit op zijn IT-systemen en beheersmaatregelen; het 8-K van 26 juni zegt dat het bedrijf een cyberverzekering heeft die volgens zijn verwachting volstaat. Het bedrijf noemde het type aanval niet publiekelijk; waarnemers vermoedden ransomware (vermoeden).
who: Nobody named.

sources.title: Cyberattack Disrupts Whole Foods Supplier, Causing Delivery Delays and Empty Shelves
Whole Foods working to restock shelves as distributor faces cyberattack
United Natural Foods cyberattack disrupts operations across North America

checked: Searched: 5 June detection, 8-K and empty shelves confirmed; added company's US$350-400M sales guidance and restoration timing (secondary sources: Teiss, Cybersecurity Dive); 'no cost figure' corrected. Whole Foods-specific restoration date not found.

service: ordering website, licence provisioning and distribution platforms (world's largest IT distributor)
duration: about a week; ordering restored region by region from 9 Jul
what: Ingram Micro's website and online ordering went down around 3 July 2025; the company later said ransomware had hit internal systems and it shut down systems as a precaution. Press reports say ordering was reactivated region by region from about 9 July. No cost figure was found.
what_nl: De website en het online bestelsysteem van Ingram Micro vielen rond 3 juli 2025 uit; het bedrijf zei later dat ransomware interne systemen had getroffen en dat het systemen preventief afsloot. Volgens de pers werd bestellen vanaf ongeveer 9 juli regio per regio hersteld. Er werd geen kostenraming gevonden.
cause: Ingram Micro said it had identified ransomware on certain internal systems, took some systems offline and notified law enforcement. Sources told BleepingComputer the access may have been through a GlobalProtect VPN; not officially confirmed.
cause_nl: Ingram Micro zei ransomware te hebben vastgesteld op bepaalde interne systemen, nam sommige systemen offline en verwittigde de politiediensten. Bronnen vertelden BleepingComputer dat de toegang mogelijk via een GlobalProtect-VPN verliep; niet officieel bevestigd.
who: BleepingComputer reported that a ransom note found on employee devices claimed to be from the SafePay group (the group's own note, as reported). Ingram Micro has not named an attacker and no authority has.

sources.title: Ingram Micro outage caused by SafePay ransomware attack
IT Giant Ingram Micro Reveals Ransomware Breach
Ingram Micro restarts orders, for some, following ransomware attack
Ingram Micro ransomware attack

checked: Searched: ransomware statement, SafePay ransom note (BleepingComputer), restoration by about 9 July confirmed. One search summary mentioned a separate Rhysida claim (SecurityWeek); not verified, not used.

service: management platforms for business customers and some consumer services
duration: about five days (restoration reported as expected around 30 July)
what: Orange said it detected a cyberattack on one of its information systems on 25 July 2025 and isolated the affected systems; the isolation measures disrupted some management services and platforms for business customers and some consumer services, mainly in France (Orange press release, 28 July). Restoration was reported as expected around 30 July (media). No cost figure was found.
what_nl: Orange zei op 25 juli 2025 een cyberaanval op een van zijn informatiesystemen te hebben vastgesteld en de getroffen systemen te hebben geïsoleerd; door die isolatie waren sommige beheerdiensten en platformen voor zakelijke klanten en enkele consumentendiensten verstoord, vooral in Frankrijk (persbericht van Orange, 28 juli). Het herstel werd volgens de media rond 30 juli verwacht. Er werd geen kostenraming gevonden.
cause: Orange confirmed a cyberattack on one of its information systems and filed a complaint on 28 July. Media report there was no evidence at that stage that customer data was extracted (secondary reporting; Orange declined further comment).
cause_nl: Orange bevestigde een cyberaanval op een van zijn informatiesystemen en diende op 28 juli klacht in. Media melden dat er op dat moment geen aanwijzingen waren dat klantgegevens waren buitgemaakt (secundaire berichtgeving; Orange wilde niet verder commentaar geven).
who: Nobody named by Orange, and no authority has named anyone.
europe: France only. A separate July 2025 data breach at Orange Belgium (reported as affecting 850,000 customers) was a data breach, not an outage; I found no source linking the two.

sources.title: Orange files a complaint concerning a security incident
Orange reports major cyberattack, warns of service disruptions
Orange France reports cyberattack disrupting business services

checked: Searched: Orange press release of 28 July found and added (official); disruption wording corrected (no 'significant'); unverified Warlock claim (aggregator only) removed; Orange Belgium link wording softened. BORDERLINE for 'serious disruption' bar: company says some business management and consumer services disrupted for a few days; kept on that basis.

service: airline IT systems, flight operations
duration: one day of major disruption (28 July); further recovery time not verified
what: A cyberattack caused a mass outage of Aeroflot's IT systems on 28 July 2025. Russia's prosecutor's office put the cancellations at more than 100 flights; counts differ by source (some reports say 108 of about 260 scheduled flights, others 60 or more). Russian experts quoted by Meduza estimated first-day losses at about 259 million roubles (an estimate, not an Aeroflot figure); another expert estimated total losses of US$10 to 50 million including recovery costs.
what_nl: Een cyberaanval veroorzaakte op 28 juli 2025 een massale uitval van de IT-systemen van Aeroflot. Het Russische openbaar ministerie sprak van meer dan 100 geschrapte vluchten; de aantallen verschillen per bron (volgens sommige berichten 108 van ongeveer 260 geplande vluchten, volgens andere minstens 60). Russische experts geciteerd door Meduza raamden het verlies op de eerste dag op ongeveer 259 miljoen roebel (een schatting, geen cijfer van Aeroflot); een andere expert raamde het totale verlies op 10 tot 50 miljoen dollar, inclusief herstelkosten.
cause: Russia's prosecutor's office said a cyberattack caused the mass outage and opened a criminal investigation (authority). The hackers claimed they destroyed about 7,000 servers and workstations; this was not independently verified.
cause_nl: Het Russische openbaar ministerie zei dat een cyberaanval de massale uitval veroorzaakte en opende een strafonderzoek (overheid). De hackers beweerden ongeveer 7.000 servers en werkstations te hebben vernietigd; dit werd niet onafhankelijk bevestigd.
who: The groups Silent Crow and the Belarusian Cyber Partisans claimed the attack as support for Ukraine (claim by the groups). No authority has named them in the sources seen.

sources.title: Cyberattack on Russian airline Aeroflot causes the cancellation of more than 100 flights
Pro-Ukraine hacktivists claim cyberattack on Aeroflot
Assessing Aeroflot's aftermath

checked: Searched: prosecutor statement, Silent Crow/Cyber Partisans claim, 259M roubles (Meduza, expert estimate) confirmed; removed unsourced '54 round trips'; flight counts shown as conflicting; added other expert loss estimate. Aeroflot itself initially called it a technical failure.

service: car production, sales and parts systems
duration: production halted about six weeks (Computer Weekly); restarted in stages from early October 2025
what: JLR shut down its IT systems after a cyber incident and paused vehicle production from 1 September 2025; the pause was extended several times and production restarted in stages from early October (RTE, 9 October). JLR reported exceptional costs of £196 million relating to the cyber incident in the quarter to 30 September 2025 (company figure; its total exceptional items of £238 million also included £42 million of redundancy costs). The independent Cyber Monitoring Centre estimated the cost to the UK economy at about £1.9 billion (central estimate, range £1.6 to 2.1 billion; an estimate, not JLR's bill).
what_nl: JLR sloot zijn IT-systemen af na een cyberincident en legde de autoproductie vanaf 1 september 2025 stil; de stilstand werd meermaals verlengd en de productie werd vanaf begin oktober in fasen herstart (RTE, 9 oktober). JLR meldde uitzonderlijke kosten van 196 miljoen pond met betrekking tot het cyberincident in het kwartaal tot 30 september 2025 (cijfer van het bedrijf; de totale uitzonderlijke posten van 238 miljoen pond omvatten ook 42 miljoen pond herstructureringskosten). Het onafhankelijke Cyber Monitoring Centre raamde de kost voor de Britse economie op ongeveer 1,9 miljard pond (centrale schatting, bandbreedte 1,6 tot 2,1 miljard pond; een schatting, niet de rekening van JLR).
cause: JLR confirmed a 'cyber incident' and shut systems as a precaution. JLR did not publish the type of attack in the sources I saw. A UK government guarantee of about £1.5 billion for the supply chain was reported by media.
cause_nl: JLR bevestigde een 'cyberincident' en sloot systemen preventief af. JLR publiceerde in de geraadpleegde bronnen het type aanval niet. Media meldden een Britse overheidsgarantie van ongeveer 1,5 miljard pond voor de toeleveringsketen.
who: The group calling itself Scattered Lapsus$ Hunters (a self-described merger of Scattered Spider, Lapsus$ and ShinyHunters) claimed responsibility. Not confirmed by JLR or an authority in the sources seen; I found no arrests tied to JLR.
europe: UK plants. Effects on Europe's supply chain were reported by media; no specific Belgian effect found.

Cyberattack drains £196m from JLR's quarterly results
Jaguar Land Rover attack to cost UK £1.9bn, say cyber monitors
Jaguar Land Rover restarts production

checked: Searched: £196M (company, within £238M exceptional items incl. £42M redundancy), CMC £1.9bn (range £1.6-2.1bn, model estimate) separated clearly; removed unverified '~£64M next quarter' and plant-by-plant restart order; £1.5bn government guarantee kept as media-reported.

service: tyre manufacturing plants in North America
duration: not verified; production halts at several plants reported as temporary
what: A cyberattack announced on 2 September 2025 disrupted Bridgestone Americas manufacturing plants, including two in Aiken County, South Carolina; the mayor of Joliette, Quebec said he believed all North American plants were affected (his belief, not confirmed by the company). Production was reported put on hold at several locations. Bridgestone described the incident as confined, said some plants were affected and were being methodically returned to full operation. No cost figure was found.
what_nl: Een cyberaanval, bekendgemaakt op 2 september 2025, verstoorde fabrieken van Bridgestone Americas, onder meer twee in Aiken County (South Carolina); de burgemeester van Joliette (Quebec) zei te geloven dat alle Noord-Amerikaanse fabrieken getroffen waren (zijn overtuiging, niet bevestigd door het bedrijf). De productie lag volgens berichten stil op meerdere locaties. Bridgestone noemde het incident beperkt, zei dat sommige fabrieken getroffen waren en stapsgewijs naar volledige werking werden teruggebracht. Er werd geen kostenraming gevonden.
cause: Bridgestone told BleepingComputer it was investigating a confined cyberattack affecting certain manufacturing plants and that no customer data or interfaces were compromised (company statement, as reported). Ransomware was not confirmed.
cause_nl: Bridgestone zei tegen BleepingComputer dat het een beperkte cyberaanval onderzocht die bepaalde fabrieken trof en dat geen klantgegevens of -koppelingen werden aangetast (verklaring van het bedrijf, zoals gemeld). Ransomware werd niet bevestigd.
who: Nobody named; no group has claimed it in the sources seen.

sources.title: Bridgestone cyberattack disrupts North American production

what: A ransomware attack on Collins Aerospace's MUSE software forced airline staff at several European airports to check passengers in manually from 19 September 2025. Collins said the disruption was limited to electronic check-in and baggage drop. AP reported Brussels cancelled about half its flights on the Monday. No cost figure was published in the sources seen.
what_nl: Een ransomware-aanval op de MUSE-software van Collins Aerospace dwong het personeel van luchtvaartmaatschappijen op meerdere Europese luchthavens vanaf 19 september 2025 om passagiers handmatig in te checken. Collins zei dat de verstoring beperkt bleef tot elektronische check-in en bagage-afgifte. Volgens AP schrapte Brussel op maandag ongeveer de helft van zijn vluchten. cause: ENISA (the EU cybersecurity agency) said the disruption was caused by a third-party ransomware incident, and Collins' parent RTX said in an SEC Form 8-K that ransomware affected systems supporting MUSE (as reported by media; filing not opened).

who: Nobody has been named. The UK National Crime Agency arrested a man in his 40s in West Sussex on suspicion of Computer Misuse Act offences; he was released on conditional bail and no charge was found in the sources seen. No ransomware group has claimed the attack; media quoted unnamed security experts linking it to the HardBit variant, which is not an official finding.
europe: Directly hit: Brussels Airport (Belgium), Heathrow, Berlin Brandenburg and Dublin.

what: Stryker disclosed to the SEC that a cyberattack on 11 March 2026 caused a global disruption of its Microsoft environment, and said its ability to process orders, manufacture and ship was disrupted. Media reported that surgeries were delayed (Cybernews). Stryker said the attack was contained to its internal Microsoft environment and that its connected medical products were safe to use. No cost figure was found.
what_nl: Stryker meldde aan de Amerikaanse beurswaakhond dat een cyberaanval op 11 maart 2026 een wereldwijde verstoring van zijn Microsoft-omgeving veroorzaakte, en zei dat zijn vermogen om bestellingen te verwerken, te produceren en te verzenden verstoord was. Media meldden dat operaties werden uitgesteld (Cybernews). Stryker zei dat de aanval beperkt bleef tot zijn interne Microsoft-omgeving en dat zijn verbonden medische producten veilig te gebruiken waren. Er werd geen kostenraming gevonden.

A source told BleepingComputer that attackers compromised a Microsoft Intune administrator account and used it to wipe almost 80,000 devices (media report from an anonymous source; Stryker has not confirmed the method). The Handala persona claimed more than 200,000 devices (claim; investigators reportedly found no evidence of data theft).
cause_nl: Stryker bevestigde een cyberincident. Een bron vertelde BleepingComputer dat de aanvallers een beheerdersaccount van Microsoft Intune binnendrongen en daarmee bijna 80.000 toestellen wisten (bericht van media op basis van een anonieme bron; Stryker heeft de methode niet bevestigd). De persona Handala beweerde meer dan 200.000 toestellen (claim; onderzoekers vonden naar verluidt geen aanwijzingen voor gegevensdiefstal).
who: Handala claimed the attack (claim). On 19 March 2026 the US Justice Department and FBI seized domains used by Handala and said Handala is a persona operated by Iran's intelligence ministry (MOIS); press reports (TechCrunch, Axios) link this to the Stryker attack, but whether the US filings name Stryker explicitly was not verified. Stryker has not named the attacker.

company: Carrefour, Monoprix and other French supermarket chains (about 700 commercial sites per France's attribution; second wave across Europe)
service: refrigeration and freezer control systems in hundreds of supermarkets
duration: overnight attack; stores discarded food; second wave on 1-2 November
where: France; second wave Belgium, Estonia, Finland, Ireland, Italy, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Portugal, Sweden
what: Overnight on 11-12 October 2026 attackers hijacked refrigeration controllers in French supermarkets, pushing freezers into defrost at up to 50°C, spoiling food and, according to media, sparking fires. Carrefour said 80 of its supermarkets were hit and Monoprix said about 5% of its stores; media estimates of the total range from about 400 to about 700 sites. A broadcaster reported EUR 270,000 of losses at two Alsace stores (not independently confirmed). A second wave on 1-2 November hit supermarkets and food businesses in at least nine European countries (Cybersecurity Dive); Kesko confirmed temperature irregularities at a few stores and Musgrave said 13 SuperValu stores in Ireland were affected.
what_nl: In de nacht van 11 op 12 oktober 2026 kaapten aanvallers de koelingsbesturing in Franse supermarkten, waardoor diepvriezers tot 50 °C ontdooiden, voedsel verloren ging en er volgens media branden ontstonden. Carrefour zei dat 80 van zijn supermarkten werden getroffen en Monoprix ongeveer 5 procent van zijn winkels; schattingen in de media voor het totaal lopen uiteen van ongeveer 400 tot ongeveer 700 vestigingen. Een omroep meldde 270.000 euro verlies bij twee winkels in de Elzas (niet onafhankelijk bevestigd). Een tweede golf op 1-2 november trof supermarkten en voedingsbedrijven in minstens negen Europese landen (Cybersecurity Dive); Kesko bevestigde temperatuurafwijkingen in enkele winkels en Musgrave zei dat 13 SuperValu-winkels in Ierland getroffen waren.
cause: Retailers confirmed a cyberattack on refrigeration controllers. France's cybersecurity agency ANSSI tied the affected systems to Danfoss controllers and said controllers from two other makers were also targeted (as reported); Danfoss said a limited number of systems were affected. Many affected units were reportedly end-of-life or ran outdated software. This was sabotage, not ransomware.
cause_nl: De winkelketens bevestigden een cyberaanval op koelingsbesturingen. Het Franse cyberveiligheidsagentschap ANSSI koppelde de getroffen systemen aan besturingen van Danfoss en zei dat ook besturingen van twee andere fabrikanten waren geviseerd (zoals gemeld); Danfoss zei dat een beperkt aantal systemen was getroffen. Veel getroffen toestellen waren naar verluidt verouderd of draaiden verouderde software. Het ging om sabotage, niet om ransomware.
who: France formally attributed the October attacks to Shahid Kaveh, a unit of Iran's Revolutionary Guards, on 9 November 2026 (foreign minister Jean-Noel Barrot); Paris prosecutors issued international arrest warrants (some outlets say requested), France summoned Iran's ambassador and will propose EU sanctions. The technical evidence has not been published and Iran denies it ('baseless and malicious'). US agencies reportedly hold only low confidence in the link (reported in the briefing's verified file; I could not re-verify). Pro-Russian groups NoName057(16) and Z-Pentest claimed the attacks on Telegram and then deleted the posts (claims); the Kremlin called Russian involvement absurd. For Belgium (1-2 November), Interior Minister Bernard Quintin said Iran was 'very likely' behind it, citing indications from the security services; Foreign Minister Maxime Prevot said the information is insufficient to hold Iran officially responsible, and the federal prosecutor declined to comment.
europe: France directly; second wave included Belgium and the Netherlands (which chains was not verified; ICA's confirmation of an attack is reported inconsistently and I found nothing on Selver).

company: Ahold Delhaize (Albert Heijn, Delhaize, Etos, Gall & Gall, Stop & Shop, Food Lion, Hannaford)
service: websites, apps and online ordering; Albert Heijn deliveries and restocking
duration: about ten days: Albert Heijn website back 19 Oct, deliveries not before 22 Oct; US sites still offline on 19 Oct and reported back online by 22 Oct
what: Ahold Delhaize said on 12 October 2026 that it had a 'security issue' in its network and was taking some systems offline; stores stayed open. Websites, apps and online ordering of several brands were disrupted, and Albert Heijn's website, app and home delivery went down. Etos, Gall & Gall, Delhaize (Belgium) and US chains were also affected. Reuters (via Teiss) reported that Albert Heijn's website returned on 19 October but online deliveries would not resume before Thursday at the earliest; AP reported the US supermarkets back online by 22 October. Retail experts estimated Albert Heijn's missed sales at EUR 120 to 150 million (an outside estimate; the company disclosed no figure).
what_nl: Ahold Delhaize zei op 12 oktober 2026 dat het een 'beveiligingsprobleem' in zijn netwerk had en bepaalde systemen offline haalde; de winkels bleven open. Websites, apps en online bestellingen van meerdere merken waren verstoord en de website, de app en de thuislevering van Albert Heijn vielen uit. Ook Etos, Gall & Gall, Delhaize (België) en de Amerikaanse ketens werden getroffen. Volgens Reuters (via Teiss) was de website van Albert Heijn op 19 oktober terug, maar zouden online leveringen ten vroegste donderdag hervat worden; volgens AP waren de Amerikaanse supermarkten op 22 oktober weer online. Retailexperts raamden de gemiste omzet van Albert Heijn op 120 tot 150 miljoen euro (een externe schatting; het bedrijf maakte geen cijfer bekend).
cause: Ahold Delhaize described a 'security issue' and said it found no evidence that sensitive customer, employee or partner data was stolen. Reuters (via Teiss) reported it informed Dutch police on 19 October. The company has not said whether attackers encrypted files or which kind of attack it was. Sources differ on the start (some say 11 October).
cause_nl: Ahold Delhaize sprak van een 'beveiligingsprobleem' en zei geen aanwijzingen te hebben dat gevoelige gegevens van klanten, personeel of partners werden gestolen. Volgens Reuters (via Teiss) verwittigde het op 19 oktober de Nederlandse politie. Het bedrijf zei niet of de aanvallers bestanden versleutelden en om welk soort aanval het ging. Bronnen verschillen over het begin (sommige zeggen 11 oktober).
who: Nobody named. In the sources seen no group has claimed it and no authority has named anyone.
europe: Directly: Albert Heijn, Etos and Gall & Gall (Netherlands) and Delhaize (Belgium, e-commerce affected).
